newsitem.title: israel: Buildings sway as quake hits Israel, Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Buildings sway as quake hits Israel, Lebanon.

text.p: Buildings swayed on Wednesday when an earthquake shook Israel and Lebanon but no injuries or serious damage were immediately reported.
Residents in the Israeli cities of Haifa and Tel Aviv said they felt their buildings move.
"My bed rocked heavily. I don't recall being that frightened since the big 1956 earthquake," a housewife in the south Lebanon port city of Sidon said.
The 1956 earthquake measured six on the open-ended scale and caused widespread damage.
Police said the Wednesday earthquake, felt across Lebanon, caused some cracks in old houses.
Yefim Gitterman, a scientist at Israel's Seismological Institute, said the 7.22 a.m. (0422 gmt) quake measured 5.5 on the Richter scale.
In Cyprus, where the tremor was not felt, the geological surveys department said the quake measured 5.6 on the Richter scale.

"We estimate it (the epicentre) was around 350 kilometres (220 miles) east of Cyprus," government geologist Kyriakos Solomi told Reuters, adding that his department was still checking the precise epicentre.
Israel's Gitterman said the quake was "short and strong" and aftershocks were felt.
Israel Radio said it was felt in Syria as well.
